sports.title: 'Indians very interested in what we do': Firouzja, youngest to beat Carlsen's record
sports.body: Alireza Firouzja discussed his ankle injury, recovery, and strong connection with Indian chess fans during an exclusive interview. He praised Indian crowds and tandoori chicken, assessed Gukesh-Sindarov’s upcoming World Championship match as close, and reflected on the difficulty of reaching the Candidates. The 23-year-old is fully recovered and will next compete in Budapest’s Total Chess Championship in November 2026.

sports.title: Harita Bhadra: India's second-fastest woman with a jewellery brand
sports.body: At 23, Bhadra is heading to her first international competition after a breakthrough domestic season that has included a 23.14-second 200m, a national indoor 60m title and an 11.22-second 100m. She will compete in the 200m and 4x100m relay at the Asian Games alongside Unnathi Bollanda. Away from athletics, Bhadra runs a handmade jewellery brand, admires Rafael Nadal and keeps her focus firmly on just one day at a time.

Ganges thrashed Mumba Masters 16-1, while Pipers beat American Gambits 9-7, with Magnus Carlsen defeating Javokhir Sindarov and handing his POTM trophy to Vidit Gujrathi. Ganges lead on game points, while Gambits need a win and help.
